passage:
Dear Customer Relations Manager,

When a passenger has a "Confirmed" ticket for a long international business trip, it should mean they have a guaranteed seat on the plane. However, my experience with your airline on March 24th showed me that this is not true. I am writing this letter to tell you that I am very unhappy with how your staff handled my flight from Toronto to London. Because of your company's mistake, I missed my next flight and had serious problems with my job.

The trouble started at the boarding gate for Flight AC882. I checked in online twenty-four hours before the flight, but the gate workers told me the plane was full. They gave my seat to another passenger who flies more often with your airline. I know that airlines often sell too many tickets, but the workers were not honest with me. They made me wait for ninety minutes without telling me anything. The agents cared more about their paperwork than talking to the four passengers who were left behind.

When they finally told me that I could not get on the plane, it was too late. I could not catch my next flight to Frankfurt. Because of this long delay, I missed an important meeting to sign a contract with a big European client. This mistake caused my business to lose a deal worth more than $15,000. Also, your staff did not give me a hotel voucher quickly. I had to find a hotel by myself and pay $340 with my own money.

The gate workers offered me a standard payment of $400, but this is not enough money for my lost time and business damage. I travel very often and I always choose your airline, but this bad service makes me feel like I cannot trust you anymore.

I want you to pay me back the $340 for my hotel room. I also want you to give me 50,000 frequent flyer miles or a $1,200 travel voucher because I lost my business meeting. I hope you will fix this problem quickly because I am a loyal business customer.

Best regards,

Marcus Thorne
